description: Implement statistical process control for a manufacturing process from characteristic selection through control chart deployment.

steps.description: Select the critical quality characteristics to monitor with SPC.

outputs.name: critical-characteristics
outputs.desc: List of CTQ characteristics to monitor

outputs.name: measurement-methods
outputs.desc: How each characteristic will be measured

process: Review product specifications and tolerances
Identify characteristics that affect fitness for use
Rank by impact on customer satisfaction and defect cost
Select measurement methods for each characteristic

steps.description: Choose the appropriate control chart type for each characteristic.

outputs.name: chart-assignments
outputs.desc: Control chart type assigned to each characteristic

outputs.name: sampling-plan
outputs.desc: Sample size, frequency, and subgroup rationale

process: Classify each characteristic as variable or attribute data
Select chart type: X-bar R, X-bar S, I-MR for variables; p, np, c, u for attributes
Define subgroup size and sampling frequency
Document the rationale for each selection

steps.description: Collect baseline data to establish initial control limits.

outputs.name: baseline-data
outputs.desc: Collected baseline measurements

outputs.name: data-quality-report
outputs.desc: Assessment of data completeness and measurement system adequacy

process: Collect at least 25 subgroups under stable conditions
Verify the measurement system is adequate (Gage R&R)
Check for special causes during baseline collection
Document the process conditions during data collection

steps.description: Calculate control limits from the baseline data.

outputs.name: control-limits
outputs.desc: UCL, CL, and LCL for each chart

outputs.name: process-capability
outputs.desc: Cp and Cpk values for each characteristic

process: Calculate center line and control limits using standard formulas
Test for normality and check assumptions
Compute Cp and Cpk against specification limits
Flag characteristics where Cpk is below 1.33

steps.description: Set up real-time control charting at the process.

inputs.name: control-limits
inputs.desc: UCL, CL, LCL for each chart

outputs.name: chart-setup-record
outputs.desc: Deployed chart configurations

outputs.name: operator-instructions
outputs.desc: Work instructions for chart maintenance

process: Configure the charting system (software or manual forms)
Set up data entry points at the workstation
Write operator instructions for sampling and plotting
Train operators on chart interpretation

steps.description: Define out-of-control response rules and reaction plans.

outputs.name: response-rules
outputs.desc: Western Electric rules and reaction plans

outputs.name: spc-implementation-plan
outputs.desc: Complete SPC program documentation

process: Define which Western Electric rules to apply (1 point beyond 3 sigma, run of 7, etc.)
Write a reaction plan for each rule violation
Define escalation paths for persistent out-of-control conditions
Compile the full SPC implementation plan

description: Map a value stream from current state through future state design to improvement implementation planning.

steps.description: Select the product family and define the value stream boundaries.

inputs.name: product-list
inputs.desc: List of products and their process routings

inputs.name: business-objectives
inputs.desc: Strategic goals for the improvement effort

outputs.name: product-family
outputs.desc: Selected product family for mapping

outputs.name: stream-boundaries
outputs.desc: Start and end points of the value stream

process: Group products by shared process steps using a product-process matrix
Select the family with the highest volume or strategic importance
Define the upstream boundary (raw material receipt) and downstream boundary (shipment)
Identify the customer and their demand rate (takt time)

steps.description: Walk the process floor and collect current state data.

outputs.name: process-data
outputs.desc: Cycle times, changeover times, uptime, inventory, batch sizes per step

outputs.name: information-flow
outputs.desc: How scheduling and production signals move

process: Walk the process from shipping back to raw material (door to door)
Record cycle time, changeover time, uptime, batch size, and operators at each step
Count inventory between each step
Map the information flow: how does each step know what to produce next

steps.description: Draw the current state value stream map.

outputs.name: current-state-map
outputs.desc: Complete current state VSM

outputs.name: timeline
outputs.desc: Lead time and value-added time calculations

process: Draw the material flow from left to right with standard VSM icons
Add the information flow across the top
Calculate lead time (sum of inventory days) and value-added time (sum of cycle times)
Compute the value-added ratio

steps.description: Identify waste and improvement opportunities in the current state.

outputs.name: waste-catalog
outputs.desc: Identified wastes categorized by type

outputs.name: improvement-opportunities
outputs.desc: Specific changes that would reduce waste

process: Walk through each step and inventory point looking for the 8 wastes
Categorize: overproduction, waiting, transport, overprocessing, inventory, motion, defects, unused talent
Quantify the cost or time impact of each waste
List improvement opportunities at each point

steps.description: Design the future state value stream map.

outputs.name: future-state-map
outputs.desc: Designed future state VSM

outputs.name: target-metrics
outputs.desc: Target lead time, VA ratio, inventory levels

process: Apply lean principles: produce to takt, implement flow where possible, use pull where flow is not possible
Design supermarket and kanban systems for remaining batch processes
Identify the pacemaker process
Draw the future state map with target metrics

steps.description: Create the implementation plan with kaizen events.

outputs.name: implementation-plan
outputs.desc: Sequenced plan with kaizen events

outputs.name: value-stream-analysis
outputs.desc: Complete VSM analysis document

process: Break the future state into implementation loops (pacemaker loop first)
Define kaizen events for each loop with scope, team, and dates
Sequence the events to build on each other
Compile the complete value stream analysis with current state, future state, and implementation plan

description: Run a Six Sigma DMAIC improvement project from problem definition through sustained control.

steps.description: Define the problem, scope, and project charter.

inputs.name: problem-statement
inputs.desc: Description of the quality or performance issue

inputs.name: business-case
inputs.desc: Why this problem matters to the business

outputs.name: project-charter
outputs.desc: DMAIC project charter with scope, goals, timeline, team

outputs.name: ctq-tree
outputs.desc: Critical to quality characteristics derived from customer needs

process: Write the problem statement in measurable terms
Define the project scope, goals, and timeline
Identify the team and stakeholders
Build the CTQ tree from voice of customer to measurable characteristics

steps.description: Measure the current process performance.

outputs.name: baseline-performance
outputs.desc: Current Cpk, sigma level, defect rate

outputs.name: measurement-plan
outputs.desc: Data collection plan and validated measurement system

process: Define the data collection plan (what, where, when, who, how)
Validate the measurement system (Gage R&R)
Collect baseline data
Calculate process capability (Cpk) and sigma level

steps.description: Analyze data to identify root causes.

outputs.name: root-causes
outputs.desc: Verified root causes with statistical evidence

outputs.name: analysis-report
outputs.desc: Statistical analysis results

process: Generate hypotheses using fishbone diagrams and process mapping
Test hypotheses with data (hypothesis tests, regression, ANOVA)
Run designed experiments (DOE) if needed to confirm factors
Document verified root causes with statistical evidence

steps.description: Develop and implement solutions for verified root causes.

outputs.name: implemented-solutions
outputs.desc: Solutions implemented with verification data

outputs.name: improved-performance
outputs.desc: Post-improvement process capability

process: Generate solution alternatives for each root cause
Evaluate and select solutions (impact, feasibility, cost)
Pilot the solutions and verify improvement with data
Implement the full-scale solutions

steps.description: Establish controls to sustain the improvement.

outputs.name: control-plan
outputs.desc: Monitoring plan with control charts and response rules

outputs.name: dmaic-project-report
outputs.desc: Complete DMAIC project report with before and after data

process: Develop the control plan (what to monitor, how, who, response rules)
Implement control charts at the process
Update standard work and training materials
Compile the DMAIC project report and hand off to process owners

description: Set up a preventive and predictive maintenance program from equipment inventory through failure analysis.

steps.description: Inventory equipment and assess criticality.

inputs.name: equipment-list
inputs.desc: List of all production and support equipment

outputs.name: criticality-ranking
outputs.desc: Equipment ranked by impact of failure

outputs.name: equipment-registry
outputs.desc: Master equipment registry with IDs and locations

process: Catalog all equipment with unique identifiers
Assess each for failure impact on safety, quality, output, and cost
Classify as critical (A), important (B), or general (C)
Prioritize maintenance effort by criticality class

steps.description: Define preventive maintenance tasks and intervals for each equipment class.

outputs.name: pm-task-list
outputs.desc: Maintenance tasks with intervals for each equipment

outputs.name: spare-parts-list
outputs.desc: Required spare parts and consumables

process: Review manufacturer recommendations for each equipment type
Incorporate failure history and operator knowledge
Define tasks: inspection, lubrication, calibration, replacement
Set intervals based on operating hours, calendar time, or condition triggers

steps.description: Configure the scheduling system for maintenance work orders.

outputs.name: scheduling-system
outputs.desc: Configured CMMS with scheduled work orders

outputs.name: work-order-templates
outputs.desc: Standard work order templates for each task type

process: Enter equipment master data into the CMMS
Create PM work order templates for each task
Set up the scheduling engine with task intervals
Configure notification and escalation rules for overdue tasks

steps.description: Train maintenance technicians on procedures and the scheduling system.

outputs.name: training-records
outputs.desc: Completed training documentation

outputs.name: procedure-manual
outputs.desc: Maintenance procedure manual

process: Write step-by-step procedures for each maintenance task
Train technicians on procedures, safety, and the CMMS system
Assess competency through practical demonstrations
Document training completion for each technician

steps.description: Track maintenance completion and equipment performance.

outputs.name: maintenance-metrics
outputs.desc: PM completion rate, MTBF, MTTR, OEE

outputs.name: equipment-uptime-report
outputs.desc: Uptime and availability by equipment

process: Track PM completion rate (target above 90%)
Calculate MTBF and MTTR for critical equipment
Compute OEE (availability x performance x quality)
Generate weekly and monthly maintenance dashboards

steps.description: Analyze failure data to improve the maintenance program.

outputs.name: failure-analysis
outputs.desc: Pareto of failure modes and root causes

outputs.name: pm-program-document
outputs.desc: Complete preventive maintenance program document

process: Run Pareto analysis on equipment failures by frequency and cost
Identify chronic failures for root cause analysis
Adjust PM intervals based on actual failure data
Compile the full PM program document with procedures, schedules, and metrics

description: Optimize a production schedule from demand collection through capacity-constrained sequencing.

steps.description: Collect demand forecasts and the order backlog.

inputs.name: order-backlog
inputs.desc: Current open orders with due dates

outputs.name: demand-plan
outputs.desc: Consolidated demand by product and time period

outputs.name: priority-rules
outputs.desc: Order priority criteria (due date, customer tier, margin)

process: Merge sales forecast with confirmed orders
Resolve conflicts between forecast and actual orders
Set priority rules for sequencing (due date, customer class, profitability)
Aggregate demand into planning time buckets

steps.description: Assess available production capacity and materials.

outputs.name: capacity-profile
outputs.desc: Available capacity by work center and period

outputs.name: material-availability
outputs.desc: Material status and shortage list

process: Calculate available capacity per work center (shifts, efficiency, planned downtime)
Check material availability against the bill of materials
Identify bottleneck work centers
Flag material shortages that will constrain the schedule

steps.description: Define scheduling constraints and sequencing rules.

outputs.name: constraint-set
outputs.desc: All scheduling constraints (changeover, sequence, batch size)

outputs.name: sequencing-rules
outputs.desc: Rules for job ordering at each work center

process: Define changeover times between product types (setup matrix)
Identify sequence-dependent constraints (color families, allergen segregation)
Set minimum and maximum batch sizes
Define operator skill requirements by work center

steps.description: Generate the production schedule using finite capacity logic.

outputs.name: draft-schedule
outputs.desc: Initial production schedule by work center

outputs.name: load-profile
outputs.desc: Capacity utilization by work center and period

process: Run the scheduling algorithm (forward or backward, finite capacity)
Load jobs to work centers respecting constraints
Resolve overloads by splitting, shifting, or outsourcing
Generate the Gantt chart and load profile

steps.description: Optimize the schedule for on-time delivery and utilization.

outputs.name: optimized-schedule
outputs.desc: Final production schedule

outputs.name: schedule-kpis
outputs.desc: On-time rate, utilization, changeover count, WIP level

process: Evaluate the draft against KPIs (on-time delivery, utilization, WIP)
Apply heuristics to reduce changeovers (batch similar products)
Balance load across parallel work centers
Verify all due dates are met or flag exceptions

steps.description: Publish the schedule and communicate to the floor.

outputs.name: published-schedule
outputs.desc: Production schedule distributed to all stakeholders

outputs.name: production-schedule-report
outputs.desc: Schedule report with KPIs and exception list

process: Format the schedule for each audience (shop floor, materials, shipping)
Distribute work orders to production supervisors
Communicate material pull signals to the warehouse
Compile the schedule report with KPIs and risk items

description: Set up an incoming material inspection program from criteria definition through supplier performance tracking.

steps.description: Define inspection criteria for each incoming material type.

inputs.name: material-specifications
inputs.desc: Specifications and tolerances for incoming materials

inputs.name: quality-history
inputs.desc: Historical quality data by material and supplier

outputs.name: inspection-criteria
outputs.desc: Criteria per material: dimensions, appearance, chemical, functional

outputs.name: risk-classification
outputs.desc: Material risk levels (critical, major, minor)

process: List all incoming material types and their specifications
Classify by risk level based on impact if nonconforming
Define specific measurements, tests, and acceptance criteria for each
Set inspection level (normal, tightened, reduced) by risk class

steps.description: Select the statistical sampling plan for each material.

outputs.name: sampling-plans
outputs.desc: AQL-based sampling plans per material

outputs.name: switching-rules
outputs.desc: Rules for switching between normal, tightened, and reduced inspection

process: Select the acceptable quality level (AQL) for each material class
Look up the sampling plan from ANSI/ASQ Z1.4 (attributes) or Z1.9 (variables)
Define the switching rules (5 consecutive lots accepted for reduced, 2 rejected for tightened)
Document the lot definition (what constitutes one lot)

steps.description: Write the inspection procedures and set up the inspection area.

outputs.name: inspection-procedures
outputs.desc: Step-by-step inspection instructions per material

outputs.name: equipment-list
outputs.desc: Required inspection tools and gages

process: Write step-by-step procedures for each material type
Specify the inspection equipment and calibration requirements
Design the inspection record forms
Set up the inspection area with adequate lighting, tools, and reference samples

steps.description: Train inspectors on procedures and measurement techniques.

outputs.name: trained-inspectors
outputs.desc: Qualified inspector roster

outputs.name: training-log
outputs.desc: Training completion records

process: Train inspectors on each procedure with hands-on practice
Conduct proficiency testing with known samples
Verify inter-inspector agreement (attribute agreement analysis)
Document qualifications and requalification schedule

steps.description: Set up the process for handling nonconforming incoming material.

outputs.name: ncr-process
outputs.desc: Nonconformance reporting and disposition process

outputs.name: quarantine-procedure
outputs.desc: Quarantine, return, rework, or use-as-is decision flow

process: Define the nonconformance report (NCR) form and workflow
Set disposition options: return to supplier, rework, use-as-is with concession, scrap
Define approval authority for each disposition (quality engineer, customer)
Set up the quarantine area and labeling system

steps.description: Track supplier quality performance over time.

outputs.name: supplier-scorecard
outputs.desc: Quality performance by supplier (lot acceptance rate, PPM)

outputs.name: incoming-inspection-protocol
outputs.desc: Complete incoming inspection protocol document

process: Track lot acceptance rate and defect PPM by supplier and material
Apply switching rules to adjust inspection levels
Generate supplier scorecards for quarterly review
Compile the complete incoming inspection protocol

description: Conduct a structured root cause analysis from problem definition through corrective action verification.

steps.description: Define the problem in measurable, specific terms.

inputs.name: impact-data
inputs.desc: Data on the scope and severity of the problem

outputs.name: problem-definition
outputs.desc: Specific, measurable problem statement (is/is-not)

outputs.name: containment-actions
outputs.desc: Immediate actions to contain the problem

process: Write the problem statement: what, where, when, how much
Construct the is/is-not analysis to bound the problem
Implement immediate containment actions to protect the customer
Define the timeline and team for the investigation

steps.description: Collect data and physical evidence related to the problem.

outputs.name: evidence-package
outputs.desc: Collected data, samples, photos, and process records

outputs.name: timeline-of-events
outputs.desc: Chronological sequence of events around the failure

process: Gather physical evidence (failed parts, samples, photos)
Collect process data (machine parameters, material lot numbers, operator logs)
Interview operators and witnesses
Build the timeline of events leading to and following the failure

steps.description: Apply root cause analysis tools to identify the root cause.

outputs.name: cause-hypotheses
outputs.desc: Candidate root causes from analysis

outputs.name: analysis-artifacts
outputs.desc: Fishbone diagrams, fault trees, 5 Why chains

process: Build a fishbone (Ishikawa) diagram with all potential causes by category
Apply 5 Why analysis to drill down from each potential cause
Build a fault tree for complex failures with multiple contributing factors
Narrow to the most likely root causes based on evidence

steps.description: Verify the root cause with data or experiment.

outputs.name: verified-root-cause
outputs.desc: Confirmed root cause with supporting evidence

outputs.name: verification-data
outputs.desc: Data or experimental results confirming the cause

process: Design tests to confirm or eliminate each candidate cause
Run the tests (reproduce the failure, or demonstrate that removing the cause prevents it)
Confirm that the verified cause explains all aspects of the is/is-not analysis
Document the evidence supporting the root cause determination

steps.description: Implement corrective actions addressing the root cause.

outputs.name: corrective-actions
outputs.desc: Implemented permanent corrective actions

outputs.name: prevention-actions
outputs.desc: Systemic changes to prevent recurrence in similar processes

process: Develop corrective actions that address the root cause directly
Develop preventive actions that address the systemic gap that allowed the cause
Implement the actions with clear ownership and timelines
Update procedures, training, and error-proofing as needed

steps.description: Verify that corrective actions are effective and the problem does not recur.

outputs.name: effectiveness-check
outputs.desc: Verification that the problem has not recurred

outputs.name: rca-report
outputs.desc: Complete root cause analysis report

process: Monitor the process for a defined period after implementation
Compare defect rates before and after corrective action
Verify the problem has not recurred and no new problems were created
Compile the complete RCA report and close the investigation

description: Conduct a Failure Mode and Effects Analysis from scope definition through action verification.

steps.description: Define the FMEA scope and assemble the team.

inputs.name: design-or-process
inputs.desc: The design or process to analyze

outputs.name: fmea-scope
outputs.desc: Defined scope, type (design or process), and team roster

outputs.name: function-list
outputs.desc: Functions and requirements of each item or step

process: Decide the FMEA type: design (DFMEA) or process (PFMEA)
Define the scope boundaries and what is included
Assemble the cross-functional team (design, manufacturing, quality, service)
List all functions and requirements of the item or process steps

steps.description: List all potential failure modes for each function.

outputs.name: failure-modes
outputs.desc: All potential failure modes by function

outputs.name: effects-list
outputs.desc: Effects of each failure mode on the system and customer

process: For each function, brainstorm how it could fail (loss, degradation, intermittent, unintended)
Describe the local and end effects of each failure mode
Identify the potential causes or mechanisms for each failure mode
Reference historical data (warranty, scrap, complaints) for known failure modes

steps.description: Score severity, occurrence, and detection for each failure mode.

outputs.name: risk-scores
outputs.desc: Severity, occurrence, detection, and RPN for each failure mode

outputs.name: ranking
outputs.desc: Failure modes ranked by RPN and severity

process: Score severity (1 to 10) based on the worst effect of the failure
Score occurrence (1 to 10) based on the likelihood of the cause
Score detection (1 to 10) based on the ability of current controls to detect before reaching the customer
Calculate RPN = severity x occurrence x detection

steps.description: Prioritize and assign actions for high-risk failure modes.

outputs.name: action-plan
outputs.desc: Recommended actions with owners and target dates

outputs.name: action-priorities
outputs.desc: Prioritized list focusing on high severity and high RPN items

process: Flag all failure modes with severity 9 or 10 regardless of RPN
Flag all failure modes with RPN above the threshold (typically 100 or 120)
Define recommended actions to reduce severity, occurrence, or detection
Assign action owners and target completion dates

steps.description: Verify implemented actions and rescore.

outputs.name: revised-scores
outputs.desc: Updated severity, occurrence, detection after actions

outputs.name: fmea-document
outputs.desc: Complete FMEA document with before and after scores

process: Verify each action was implemented as planned
Rescore severity, occurrence, and detection after implementation
Calculate the revised RPN
Compile the FMEA document as a living document for future updates

description: Set up an ISO 9001 quality management system from scope definition through management review.

steps.description: Define the QMS scope, quality policy, and quality objectives.

inputs.name: organization-context
inputs.desc: Products, markets, interested parties, regulatory requirements

outputs.name: qms-scope
outputs.desc: Defined scope of the quality management system

outputs.name: quality-policy
outputs.desc: Quality policy statement and measurable objectives

process: Identify the organization's context and interested parties (clause 4)
Define the scope: which products, processes, and locations are included
Draft the quality policy aligned with strategic direction
Set measurable quality objectives with targets and timelines

steps.description: Map the organization's processes and their interactions.

outputs.name: process-map
outputs.desc: Process interaction diagram (turtle diagrams or SIPOC)

outputs.name: process-owners
outputs.desc: Assigned process owners for each process

process: Identify all processes within the QMS scope
Classify as management, core (realization), or support processes
Define inputs, outputs, resources, and controls for each process
Map the interactions between processes

steps.description: Write procedures, work instructions, and forms.

outputs.name: documented-procedures
outputs.desc: Required procedures and work instructions

outputs.name: forms-and-records
outputs.desc: Record templates for each process

process: Write mandatory documented information required by ISO 9001
Write procedures for each core process in a consistent format
Create work instructions for critical operations
Design forms and record templates for objective evidence

steps.description: Set up the document control system.

outputs.name: document-control-system
outputs.desc: Controlled document repository with revision management

outputs.name: control-procedure
outputs.desc: Document and record control procedure

process: Select the document management platform
Define the numbering, revision, and approval workflow
Load all documents and assign access permissions
Obsolete or archive superseded documents

steps.description: Implement the internal audit program.

outputs.name: audit-schedule
outputs.desc: Annual internal audit schedule covering all processes

outputs.name: auditor-qualifications
outputs.desc: Trained internal auditor roster

process: Build the annual audit schedule covering all processes and clauses
Train internal auditors on ISO 19011 audit principles
Develop audit checklists for each process
Define the nonconformity and corrective action workflow for audit findings

steps.description: Conduct the management review and compile the QMS manual.

outputs.name: management-review-record
outputs.desc: Management review minutes and decisions

outputs.name: qms-manual
outputs.desc: Complete quality management system manual

process: Prepare management review inputs (audit results, customer feedback, process performance, risks)
Conduct the review with top management
Record decisions and action items (resource needs, improvements, policy changes)
Compile the QMS manual referencing all procedures and the process interaction diagram

description: Qualify a new supplier from criteria definition through approval decision.

steps.description: Define the criteria for supplier qualification.

inputs.name: material-requirements
inputs.desc: Specifications for the material or component to be supplied

inputs.name: quality-standards
inputs.desc: Required certifications and quality system standards

outputs.name: qualification-criteria
outputs.desc: Weighted scoring criteria (quality, delivery, cost, capacity, certifications)

outputs.name: evaluation-scorecard
outputs.desc: Blank scorecard template for assessment

process: Define the quality requirements (specifications, defect limits, process capability)
Define delivery requirements (lead time, on-time rate, flexibility)
Define capacity and financial stability requirements
Weight the criteria by importance and create the scoring template

steps.description: Send the supplier self-assessment questionnaire.

inputs.name: candidate-suppliers
inputs.desc: List of candidate suppliers to evaluate

outputs.name: questionnaire-responses
outputs.desc: Completed questionnaires from candidate suppliers

outputs.name: document-submissions
outputs.desc: Certifications, quality manuals, and references submitted

process: Prepare the supplier questionnaire covering all criteria areas
Send to candidate suppliers with submission deadline
Collect responses and supporting documentation
Screen responses for minimum requirements (disqualify if not met)

steps.description: Conduct the on-site supplier audit.

outputs.name: audit-findings
outputs.desc: On-site audit observations, conformances, and nonconformances

outputs.name: process-capability-data
outputs.desc: Observed process capability and capacity data

process: Prepare the audit checklist from the questionnaire responses and criteria
Conduct the on-site audit (quality system, production processes, capacity)
Verify claimed certifications and calibration records
Document findings: conformances, observations, minor and major nonconformances

steps.description: Evaluate sample parts from the candidate supplier.

outputs.name: sample-evaluation
outputs.desc: Test results and dimensional data from sample parts

outputs.name: ppap-package
outputs.desc: Production Part Approval Process documentation if applicable

process: Request sample parts produced on production tooling and processes
Inspect and test against all specification requirements
Evaluate dimensional data, material certifications, and functional test results
Review the PPAP or equivalent first article package

steps.description: Make the qualification decision and onboard the supplier.

outputs.name: qualification-decision
outputs.desc: Approved, conditionally approved, or rejected

outputs.name: supplier-qualification-report
outputs.desc: Complete qualification report with all evidence

process: Score the supplier on the evaluation scorecard across all criteria
Review audit nonconformances and corrective action adequacy
Make the qualification decision (approved, conditional, rejected)
Set up the supplier in the approved supplier list with any conditions or monitoring requirements

description: Manage a corrective action from problem description through closure using the 8D methodology.

steps.description: Initiate the corrective action with problem description and containment.

inputs.name: nonconformance-report
inputs.desc: NCR or customer complaint triggering the action

outputs.name: ca-record
outputs.desc: Corrective action record with problem description (D1-D3)

outputs.name: containment-status
outputs.desc: Interim containment actions in place

process: Open the corrective action record and assign a unique number
Form the team with relevant expertise (D1)
Describe the problem in specific, quantified terms (D2)
Implement interim containment actions to protect the customer (D3)

steps.description: Identify and verify the root cause.

outputs.name: verified-cause
outputs.desc: Root cause verified with data (D4)

outputs.name: escape-point
outputs.desc: Where the defect escaped detection

process: Identify all possible causes using structured tools (fishbone, 5 Why)
Test each candidate cause against the evidence
Verify the root cause: demonstrate it reproduces the problem and removing it prevents it (D4)
Identify the escape point: why did existing controls not catch it

steps.description: Develop and verify permanent corrective actions.

outputs.name: permanent-actions
outputs.desc: Selected permanent corrective actions (D5-D6)

outputs.name: verification-results
outputs.desc: Data confirming actions address the root cause

process: Brainstorm permanent corrective actions for the root cause and the escape point
Select the best actions based on effectiveness, feasibility, and risk of side effects (D5)
Implement the permanent corrective actions (D6)
Verify with data that the actions eliminate the problem without creating new issues

steps.description: Prevent recurrence and extend to similar processes.

outputs.name: prevention-actions
outputs.desc: Systemic prevention actions (D7)

outputs.name: horizontal-deployment
outputs.desc: Similar products or processes where the same fix was applied

process: Identify systemic changes to prevent recurrence (update FMEA, control plan, procedures)
Identify similar products, processes, or plants where the same risk exists
Deploy the corrective action horizontally to those areas
Update training materials and error-proofing devices

steps.description: Verify effectiveness and close the corrective action.

outputs.name: effectiveness-verification
outputs.desc: Confirmation of sustained improvement over monitoring period

outputs.name: corrective-action-report
outputs.desc: Complete 8D report (D8)

process: Monitor the process for the defined effectiveness period (typically 60 to 90 days)
Verify that the problem has not recurred
Recognize the team (D8)
Close the corrective action record and archive the 8D report

description: Analyze a measurement system using Gage R&R to determine if it is adequate for its intended use.

steps.description: Design the Gage R&R study.

inputs.name: measurement-system
inputs.desc: The gage, fixture, and method to evaluate

inputs.name: tolerance
inputs.desc: Specification tolerance for the measured characteristic

outputs.name: study-design
outputs.desc: Crossed or nested design with operators, parts, and repeats

outputs.name: data-collection-form
outputs.desc: Form for recording measurements

process: Select the study type: crossed (all operators measure all parts) or nested
Select the number of operators (typically 3), parts (typically 10), and repeats (typically 3)
Select parts that span the process range
Prepare the data collection form with randomized measurement order

steps.description: Collect the measurements following the study design.

outputs.name: measurement-data
outputs.desc: All measurements by operator, part, and replicate

outputs.name: collection-notes
outputs.desc: Any deviations from the study plan

process: Ensure the gage is calibrated before the study
Have each operator measure each part in random order without seeing previous results
Record all measurements on the data collection form
Note any anomalies or deviations from the study plan

steps.description: Calculate repeatability, reproducibility, and total Gage R&R.

outputs.name: grr-results
outputs.desc: Repeatability, reproducibility, part variation, and total GRR

outputs.name: variance-components
outputs.desc: ANOVA variance component breakdown

process: Run the ANOVA method to decompose total variation into components
Calculate equipment variation (repeatability) and appraiser variation (reproducibility)
Compute the operator-by-part interaction
Calculate %GRR as a percentage of tolerance and as a percentage of total variation

steps.description: Assess whether the measurement system is acceptable.

outputs.name: acceptability-decision
outputs.desc: Acceptable (under 10%), marginal (10-30%), or unacceptable (over 30%)

outputs.name: number-of-distinct-categories
outputs.desc: NDC value (must be 5 or greater)

process: Apply the acceptance criteria: under 10% GRR is acceptable, 10-30% is marginal, over 30% is unacceptable
Calculate the number of distinct categories (NDC): must be 5 or greater
Identify the dominant source of variation (repeatability vs reproducibility)
Determine if the system can distinguish between parts

steps.description: Recommend improvements if the measurement system is not acceptable.

outputs.name: improvement-recommendations
outputs.desc: Actions to improve repeatability or reproducibility

outputs.name: msa-report
outputs.desc: Complete measurement system analysis report

process: If repeatability dominates: investigate gage condition, fixturing, measurement technique
If reproducibility dominates: investigate operator training, procedure clarity, environmental factors
Recommend specific actions and plan a follow-up study after implementation
Compile the complete MSA report with data, charts, and conclusions
